items.title: [Bug] DFlash2/DSpark + prefix caching corrupt output after a cache hit on Qwen3.8-27B (TP=1) on 0.30/0.31; 0.29 and MTP are fine
items.body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM 0.31.0 (also reproduced on 0.30.0). vLLM 0.29.0 passes the same test.
- torch 2.13.0+cu130, flashinfer-python/cubin 0.7.0.post1 (0.6.18.post1 on 0.30.0), CUDA 13.3, driver 610.57.04
- 1× RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell 48 GB (sm_120), Ubuntu 24.04, kernel 7.0.0-34
- Target: `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B` NVFP4 checkpoint, compressed-tensors mixed precision (NVFP4 on the MLP projections, FP8 W8A8 on attention / GDN projections / lm_head, `linear_attn.{in_proj_a,in_proj_b,norm}` and `mtp.*` unquantized via `ignore`)
- Drafter: `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` (`DFlash2DraftModel`, sliding_window 2048), `num_speculative_tokens: 7`

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Since 0.30.0, serving Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 with the DFlash2 drafter and prefix caching enabled produces garbage after a prefix-cache hit. The first requests of a conversation are fine. From the third request on, once the prompt resumes from cached blocks, the model emits a single repeated token (`duct`, over and over) with no coherent content, and the drafter accepts nothing (`SpecDecoding metrics: Mean acceptance length: 1.00, Accepted: 0 tokens`). The same five requests against 0.29.0 come back coherent every time. I have run the comparison twice on each version.

The test is a replay of a real agent conversation: five consecutive chat-completions requests from one session (31,776 / 45,606 / 52,737 / 65,364 / 67,502 prompt tokens, 25 tool schemas, seed 17), sent in order to a fresh engine so each request hits the previous one's prefix. The conversation itself is private, but I can build a synthetic equivalent if that helps.

Serve command (production flags):

```
vllm serve /models/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 --max-model-len 250000 --kv-cache-memory-bytes 17379961324 \
  --max-num-seqs 32 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"/models/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2","num_speculative_tokens":7}' \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --override-generation-config '{"temperature":1.0,"top_p":0.95,"top_k":20,"min_p":0.0}' --scheduling-policy priority
```

env: `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0 VLLM_ENFORCE_STRICT_TOOL_CALLING=false`. Prefix caching on (default), `mamba_cache_mode` resolves to `align`.

### What I tried, to narrow it down

All on 0.31.0, same five requests, fresh engine each time:

| Change | Result |
|---|---|
| nothing (command above) | fails at request 3 |
| PR #57128 applied (the `MambaManager.find_longest_cache_hit` / `drop_eagle_block` fix) | fails |
| `--gdn-prefill-backend triton` instead of FlashInfer | fails |
| `--linear-backend cutlass` (in-tree CUTLASS NVFP4 GEMM) | fails |
| `--linear-backend marlin` (weight-only W4A16, no activation quant) | fails |
| smaller KV pool / 180K window / util 0.94 (copied from my FP8 route) | fails |
| `"disable_eagle_block_drop": true` in the speculative config | worse: garbage from request 1, even cold |
| **no speculative config at all** | **passes 5/5** |
| **`{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}` (checkpoint's own MTP head)** | **passes 5/5** |
| **`{"method":"dspark","model":"RedHatAI/Qwen3.8-27B-speculator.dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7}`** | **fails at request 3** |
| **FP8 target (`Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8`, `quant_method: fp8`) with the same DFlash2 config** | **passes 5/5, twice** |

A unique `cache_salt` per request on 0.30.0 also makes requests 3–5 pass, so the failure needs an actual cache hit.

So the NVFP4 GEMM kernels are not involved (three different kernels, including weight-only, all fail), the GDN prefill kernel is not involved, and the KV pool size is not involved. What it needs is: a hidden-state drafter (DFlash2 or DSpark; MTP is fine) + a prefix-cache hit + this compressed-tensors NVFP4 target, on 0.30 or later. The FP8 checkpoint with the identical drafter config is fine. Turning off the EAGLE trailing-block drop makes it strictly worse, which reads to me like the drafter is leaving bad Mamba/GDN state in the cached tail block and the drop normally hides it inside a request but not across requests.

The compressed-tensors checkpoint is the obvious difference from the FP8 one: it has an `ignore` list covering `linear_attn` sub-modules (the bf16 `in_proj_a` / `in_proj_b` / `norm`) alongside `config_groups` that target `linear_attn.{in_proj_qkv,in_proj_z,out_proj}` at FP8. If the drafter path resolves those layers differently from the plain `fp8` loader, that would be where I'd look first, but I haven't gone further than the table above.

Related: #53912 and #55766 describe neighbouring hybrid-GDN prefix-cache corruption with speculative decoding.

### What I can provide

Per-request replay output (prompt token counts, finish reasons, draft metrics), engine logs for every ablation above, and a synthetic reproducer on request.

items.title: [Bug]: GLM-5.2-FP8 + prefix caching + FP8 KV cache returns empty content (gibberish reasoning) on repeated identical prompts
items.body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py, reconstructed from startup ```text ============================== vLLM Version ============================== vLLM Version : 0.27.1 (V1 engine; system_fingerprint "vllm-0.27.1-tp8-...") ============================== Model / Serving ============================== Model : zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8 (GlmMoeDsa, sparse-MLA / sparse_attn_indexer) served_model_name : zai-org--glm-5.2-fp8 dtype : torch.bfloat16 quantization : fp8 kv_cache_dtype : fp8_e4m3 tensor_parallel_size : 8 pipeline_parallel_size : 1 max_model_len : 524288 max_num_seqs : 32 gpu_memory_utilization : 0.8 enforce_eager : False cudagraph_mode : FULL_AND_PIECEWISE enable_prefix_caching : True enable_chunked_prefill : True speculative_config : None # no MTP / speculative decoding reasoning_parser : glm45 tool_call_parser : glm47 enable_auto_tool_choice : True moe_backend : aiter linear_backend : aiter custom_ops : ['+quant_fp8','+grouped_topk','+sparse_attn_indexer', ...] ============================== Hardware / Platform ============================== GPU : AMD Instinct MI300X x8 (ROCm / AITER backends) Engine image : hf-vllm-v0-27-1-amd (AMD build) ============================== Notable startup log lines ============================== [cache.py:296] Using fp8_e4m3 data type to store kv cache. ... it may cause accuracy drop without a proper scaling factor [mla_attention.py:522] Sparse MLA impl has no dense-MHA prefill path; using the top-k MQA path only. ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug ## 🐛 Bug Sending the **same** ~43k-token request repeatedly: first N (fresh prefill) are correct, then once it hits the prefix cache a response comes back with `content: null`, an **incoherent multilingual `reasoning`** field, and `finish_reason: "stop"` — silent, no traceback. Prepending a unique prefix (forces fresh prefill) → **0/50 failures**. So the trigger is **prefix-cache reuse**, not length, parsing, weights, or MTP. ### Repro ```bash vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8 --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --max-model-len 524288 --max-num-seqs 32 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 --enable-prefix-caching \ --reasoning-parser glm45 --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser glm47 ``` ```python import json import urllib.request import uuid BASE = "http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions" MODEL = "zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8" SYS = ( "You are an interactive agent. Prefer dedicated file tools over shell. " "Before writing a file you MUST load the design skill. External scripts " "load only from approved CDNs. Never impersonate a real person or " "organization. " ) * 350 def body(system): return { "model": MODEL, "messages": [ {"role": "system", "content": system}, {"role": "user", "content": "hi"}, ], "max_tokens": 4000, "temperature": 0, "stream": False, } def call(payload): req = urllib.request.Request( BASE, data=json.dumps(payload).encode(), headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}, ) return json.loads(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=180).read()) def classify(message): content = (message.get("content") or "").strip() return "EMPTY" if content == "" else "ok" print("identical (cache hits):") for i in range(1, 300): out = call(body(SYS)) msg = out["choices"][0]["message"] label = classify(msg) print(i, label, out["usage"]["completion_tokens"]) if label != "ok": print(json.dumps(msg, ensure_ascii=False)[:600]) break print("unique prefix (fresh prefill):") for i in range(1, 51): out = call(body(uuid.uuid4().hex + SYS)) print(i, classify(out["choices"][0]["message"])) ``` ### Observed **Identical prompt (prefix-cache hits)** — fails on the 13th request: ```text identical (cache hits): [012] ok completion_tokens=85 [013] EMPTY completion_tokens=129 ``` The failing response: `content` is null and `reasoning` is gibberish, yet `finish_reason` is `"stop"`: ```json { "role": "assistant", "content": null, "reasoning": ", samoch3,1columnfk7help\">9 ... 、seb0 might8ひ7-" } ``` **Unique prefix (fresh prefill)** — all clean: ```text unique prefix (fresh prefill): [001] ok ... [050] ok # 50/50 clean ``` ## Expected A prefix-cache hit must not corrupt generation; repeated identical requests should return consistent, coherent output. ## Suspected area Prefix-cache reuse + `fp8_e4m3` KV cache + sparse-MLA top-k MQA prefill under CUDA graphs. Can A/B `--enforce-eager`, bf16 KV, or prefix caching off if useful. ## Potentially Related #59926 (v0.27.1, fp8 KV, prefix-cache reuse; cache_salt helps — closest), #50881 (FP8 KV garbage under CUDA graphs), #60174 (prefix-cache hit corrupts output). ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.title: [Bugfix] MambaManager.find_longest_cache_hit ignores drop_eagle_block, silent corruption with prefix caching + MTP/EAGLE
items.body:
<!-- AI-assisted PR: drafted and tested with Claude (Anthropic) assistance, reviewed and submitted by the author. -->

## Purpose

`MambaManager.find_longest_cache_hit` (`vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py`) accepts `drop_eagle_block` as a parameter but never acts on it. When native MTP/EAGLE speculative decoding is combined with `--enable-prefix-caching` on a hybrid Mamba/GDN model, a matched block containing recurrent state written over rejected draft positions stays reachable through the prefix cache and gets reused by later requests sharing that prefix. This causes silent corruption (empty or repeated-character output, no error, no crash) -- matches #53912.

The root cause is also visible in `kv_cache_coordinator.py`: the coordinator deliberately skips the eagle_margin for `MambaSpec` groups, with a comment explaining *why* it doesn't need to (`MambaManager`'s own finder is expected to apply the drop) -- but the finder never did.

An earlier, simpler fix (#43650) addressed an older version of this function by pre-shrinking the search ceiling by one unit before scanning. That approach doesn't carry over to the current, rewritten `find_longest_cache_hit`: in `mamba_cache_mode="align"`, real state checkpoints only exist at sparse block boundaries, not at every fine-grained hash unit, so pre-shrinking the ceiling reliably lands in a gap between checkpoints and yields **0% cache-hit-rate** (confirmed live, see Test Plan).

## Fix

Mirror `FullAttentionManager`'s drop semantics, adapted to Mamba's snapshot (not chained-block) write model: scan the full, unrestricted window, and skip only the *first* (most recent) checkpoint actually found when `drop_eagle_block` is set, then keep scanning for the next (older, already-committed) one. This excludes exactly the one block that may hold unverified draft state, without blanking the whole tail of the search window. Applied to both the fine-grained and coarse-grained branches of the function.

`kv_cache_coordinator.py` only needed a comment update (no logic change) -- the coordinator's existing choice to skip the eagle_margin for Mamba groups was already correct, it just documented the wrong reason.

## Test Plan

- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check`: clean.
- New unit tests in `tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py` covering `MambaManager.find_longest_cache_hit` with `drop_eagle_block=True/False`, through both the coarse and fine-grained branches, plus the single-checkpoint edge case (drop must fall back to no hit, never a corrupted match). Passed locally (Python 3.12, CPU-only, `torch==2.8.0` + `requirements/common.txt`).
- Live end-to-end test against a real hybrid Mamba/GDN model:
  - **Hardware**: 2x NVIDIA RTX 5060 Ti 16GB (TP=2)
  - **Image**: `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.29.0-cu129`
  - **Model**: Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 (hybrid linear-attention/full-attention, `full_attention_interval=4`, native MTP head)
  - **Config**: `--kv-cache-dtype turboquant_4bit_nc`, `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}'`, `--enable-prefix-caching`, `--max-model-len 131072`
  - Before this fix: `--enable-prefix-caching` + MTP together gave 0% prefix-cache-hit-rate (the pre-shrink approach) or corruption risk (with drop_eagle_block unhandled).
  - With this fix: confirmed real cache hits under concurrent shared-prefix load (8 concurrent requests, ~4.4k shared prefix, no corruption in repeated correctness checks) and on a larger, more realistic shared prefix (~24k tokens): warm requests dropped from ~77s (cold) to ~30-32s, with instrumented logging confirming a genuine partial hit of 15,440 of ~18,528 available tokens (5 of 7 candidate blocks, correctly skipping the most recent/unverified one).

## Test Result

All new and existing tests pass. Live smoke tests show no corruption and a real cache-hit speedup on realistic shared-prefix traffic.

<!--
Before submitting a PR, please read the checklist below and ensure the PR has met all of them.
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation (comment update in kv_cache_coordinator.py)
-->

items.title: [Bug]: prefix caching + MTP still corrupts output on hybrid Mamba/GDN models in v0.28.0 (#43559 closed but unfixed)
items.body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text ============================== System Info ============================== OS : Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (x86_64) GCC version : (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0 Libc version : glibc-2.39 ============================== PyTorch Info ============================== PyTorch version : 2.13.0+cu130 Is debug build : False CUDA used to build PyTorch : 13.0 ROCM used to build PyTorch : N/A ============================== Python Environment ============================== Python version : 3.12.3 (main, Jun 19 2026, 12:46:00) [GCC 13.3.0] (64-bit runtime) Python platform : Linux-6.8.0-1010-gcp-x86_64-with-glibc2.39 ============================== CUDA / GPU Info ============================== Is CUDA available : True CUDA runtime version : 12.0.140 GPU models and configuration : GPU 0-7: NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (single GPU used for this report, TP=1) Nvidia driver version : 580.173.02 ============================== CPU Info ============================== Architecture: x86_64 Model name: Intel(R) Xeon(R) Platinum 8481C CPU @ 2.70GHz CPU(s): 208 Hypervisor vendor: KVM ============================== vLLM Info ============================== vLLM Version : 0.28.0 vLLM Build Flags: CUDA Archs: Not Set; ROCm: Disabled; XPU: Disabled GPU Topology: NV18 all-to-all (8x H100 SXM), TP=1 used Relevant packages: vllm==0.28.0 torch==2.13.0 transformers==5.15.1 flashinfer-python==0.6.16.post3 compressed-tensors==0.17.0 xgrammar==0.2.3 ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug **Summary.** `--enable-prefix-caching` together with MTP speculative decoding still corrupts output on hybrid (GDN/Mamba) Qwen3.5-class models in **v0.28.0**. A small fraction of responses degenerate into repeated punctuation (`!!!!…`) or come back empty. This is the same failure as #43559, which was closed as completed on 2026-08-06 — the merged scheduler-side fix (#51113) does not cover it, and the cache-manager-side fixes (#43650, #48375) are still open. **Model.** Qwen3.5-architecture dense 27B VLM (`Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`, hybrid: Gated DeltaNet linear-attention layers + full attention every 4th layer, vision tower), FP8 W8A8 compressed-tensors (`FP8_DYNAMIC`), with an MTP head present in the checkpoint (`Qwen3_5MTP` resolves at startup). TP=1, single H100. **Server command** (paths redacted): ```bash export VLLM_NO_USAGE_STATS=1 export VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 vllm serve \ --served-model-name path-mini \ --port 8000 \ --max-model-len 62768 \ --max-num-seqs 32 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \ --enable-chunked-prefill \ --limit-mm-per-prompt.image 10 \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --mamba-cache-mode align \ --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 2}' ``` Startup confirms the configuration: `Resolved architecture: Qwen3_5MTP`, `enable_prefix_caching=True`, `num_spec_tokens=2`, `GPU KV cache size: 576,637 tokens`, attention block size 800 (forced up to match the mamba page size), async scheduling enabled (default). **Workload.** Multi-step GUI-agent traces: each request is a conversation of prior steps plus 1–3 screenshots (sliding 2-image history), ~4k–12k prompt tokens, ~20–100 output tokens, `temperature=0`, client concurrency up to 32. Consecutive steps of the same episode share a long prefix, so prefix-cache hit rate climbs through a run. **Observed.** | vLLM | prefix caching | MTP | final prefix-cache hit rate | malformed responses | |---|---|---|---|---| | 0.26.0 | on | k=2 | 27.5% | 25 / 2,636 (0.95%) | | **0.28.0** | **on** | **k=2** | **31.7%** | **4 / 495 (0.81%)** | | 0.28.0 | on | k=2, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` | ~10% (see note) | 0 / 1,135 | Malformed = response is a run of repeated `!` characters, or empty content. `finish_reason` is normal; no HTTP 5xx, no crash, no traceback — the engine stays healthy and every other response in the same run is correct. Two observations that point at the prefix cache rather than at MTP alone: 1. **Rate tracks cache hit rate.** Corruption appears only once the prefix cache starts hitting, and scales with the hit rate. 2. **`--kv-cache-dtype fp8` appears to avoid it, but only by destroying the cache.** With fp8 KV, vLLM raises the attention block size 800 → 1600 (`platforms/interface.py`, so that one attention page covers one mamba page). Our requests share ~1,700 tokens of prefix, so at a 1600-token matching unit almost nothing is reusable: hit rate collapses from 31.7% to ~10%, and malformed responses go to 0/1,135. That is consistent with reduced exposure, not with fp8 fixing the underlying defect. (For the same reason `--block-size 800` cannot be used to compensate: the value is derived and only ever raised.) **Suspected cause** (already described in #43650 / #48375): `MambaManager.find_longest_cache_hit` in `vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py` accepts `drop_eagle_block` and never acts on it, so the final matched block — which can hold recurrent state written over draft positions that verification later rejected — stays reachable through the prefix cache and is reused by subsequent requests sharing that prefix. `FullAttentionManager` drops that block. In v0.28.0 the caller (`kv_cache_coordinator.py`) additionally skips the eagle margin for `MambaSpec` with the comment *"its finder never drops"*, i.e. caller and manager disagree about who is responsible. Applying **#43650** (6 lines, `max_num_blocks -= 1` when `use_eagle`) on top of v0.28.0 starts cleanly and shows no regression on an unrelated accuracy check (100 grounding requests at concurrency 32: 76% vs 75% unpatched, identical coordinate error, 0 malformed). Other users report it resolving the symptom outright (#43650: 18/39 → 39/39 on a private benchmark; `content: null` at ~1-in-8 fixed completely). **Expected.** `--enable-prefix-caching` + MTP on a hybrid Mamba/GDN model should be either correct or explicitly rejected at startup, not silently corrupting a fraction of responses. **Notes / questions** - Was #43559 closed by #51113 intentionally? #51113 fixes chunk alignment on the write path; the reports above (and this one) are about block dropping on the cache-read path, which neither #51113 nor #46384 appears to cover. - If #43650 is considered too blunt because a hybrid block can be 1k+ tokens, would a narrower fix be acceptable — e.g. dropping the trailing block only when that block actually contains unverified draft positions? - Happy to run any specific probe on this configuration; we can reproduce on demand with the workload above. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.title: [Bug]: Explicit --enable-prefix-caching with MTP spec decode + tool calling corrupts tool-call emission on repeated identical prompts
items.body:
### Your current environment

`collect_env` was not available on this host — abridged environment:

- vLLM: **0.23.0** (venv install)
- GPU: **NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090** (32,607 MiB), driver **595.71.05**, CUDA **13.0**
- `FLASHINFER_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=12.0f`, `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True`
- Model: local **Qwen3.6-27B-Text NVFP4** checkpoint (ModelOpt quantization) with MTP

Launch command (failing configuration):

```bash
vllm serve ~/models/Qwen3.6-27B-Text-NVFP4-MTP \
    --port 8000 \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --quantization modelopt \
    --language-model-only \
    --max-model-len 204800 \
    --max-num-seqs 6 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \
    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
    --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \
    --enable-prefix-caching \
    --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}'
```

The **passing** configuration is identical except `--enable-prefix-caching` is removed.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

**Summary:** with prefix caching explicitly enabled alongside MTP speculative decoding, fp8 KV cache, and the `qwen3_coder` tool-call parser, **repeated byte-identical tool-calling requests intermittently return raw, malformed tool-call markup in `message.content` with no `tool_calls` array** — near-instantly, suggesting cache-hot generation degrades (or the tool-parser path is bypassed). First-time prompts never failed. Removing `--enable-prefix-caching` eliminates the failure completely.

**Workload:** an agentic tool-calling loop against the OpenAI-compatible server — `POST /v1/chat/completions` with a system prompt, a user message, and ~13 tool schemas; multi-turn tool-use conversations. An evaluation suite runs each of 6 agent scenarios **twice** with byte-identical initial requests.

**Observed (prefix caching enabled):**
- All 6 first runs: clean — proper `tool_calls`, healthy durations (20–65 s).
- 3 of 6 repeat runs: response in **1.4–3.5 s** with tiny output; `message.content` contains raw tool-syntax the parser never transformed, no `tool_calls`. Samples from three separate failures:

```
<tool_code><function_code></function_code><parameters>{"include_income": false}</parameters><tool_name>recurring_list</tool_name>…
```
```
<call>
```
```
<tool_call><tool_call>{"name": "spending_by_category"</name></tool_call>…
```

**Observed (prefix caching disabled, same everything else):** 12/12 runs clean, including all byte-identical repeats. MTP was enabled in both configurations, so prefix caching is the discriminating variable (untested: caching on + MTP off, so an interaction is possible but unattributed).

**Disabled-state verification:** in the passing configuration, `/metrics` shows `vllm:prefix_cache_queries_total` remaining `0.0` under traffic (identical repeated prompts included) — i.e., with this feature combination, prefix caching appears to be **off by default** in 0.23.0, and the failures only occur when it is explicitly enabled. If the default is off due to a known incompatibility, an explicit `--enable-prefix-caching` seemingly bypasses that guard silently; if the combination is meant to be supported, this looks like a cache-path correctness bug.

**Possibly related (same feature pairing, different symptom):** #47930 (draft acceptance collapse with automatic prefix caching), #5543 (prefix caching inconsistent completions).

### Reproduction sketch

1. Serve the model with the failing command above (prefix caching + MTP + fp8 KV cache + `qwen3_coder` tool parser).
2. Send a chat-completions request with tool schemas; let a normal multi-turn tool loop complete.
3. Minutes later, re-send the byte-identical initial request. Intermittently (~50% of repeats in our suite), the response is near-instant garbage tool-syntax in `content` with no `tool_calls`.

Happy to provide full request payloads and per-run traces on request.

items.title: kv-cache: honor scheduler lookahead in mamba align-mode allocation
items.body:
## Problem

In mamba align cache mode (mamba-hybrid models with prefix caching), `MambaManager.allocate_new_blocks` and `get_num_blocks_to_allocate` discarded all lookahead tokens by resetting `num_tokens` to `num_tokens_main_model`. When the scheduler schedules lookahead capacity beyond a main-model sequence that ends exactly on a page boundary, this corrupts the recurrent state in two ways.

## Root cause

A mamba state table row is page-indexed: the worker's running-state column is `cdiv(main_end, bs) - 1`.

1. **Missing next page.** When a chunk ends exactly on a page boundary and lookahead tokens extend beyond it, the next page was not materialized with the current schedule. The boundary token's state write then targeted a block-table entry that still held a recycled stale block — the recurrent state is corrupted from that point on (one-step NaN followed by a repetition lock at every page boundary).

2. **Displaced running-state column.** If a page was materialized for the lookahead, the null padding was derived from the inflated `num_tokens`, so the reserved page displaced the real running-state column. The worker's running-state index (0 for a chunk ending at the first page boundary) pointed at the null slot; the next chunk's state pre-copy chained from the null slot and spec-decode acceptance collapsed to zero permanently for that request.

## Diagnosis

Reproduced on a 4-node Arm (Thor SM110) cluster serving GLM-5.3-Flash (mamba-hybrid + MTP + prefix caching) with deterministic single-turn probes: prompts whose prefill chunk ends exactly on a page boundary produced 0% spec-decode acceptance from the first decode step, while boundary-crossing-free prompts were healthy. The failure moved with cache layout across boots, and per-request scheduler dumps of the mamba state-table rows showed the displaced null column exactly at the worker's running-state index. The corruption was confirmed to chain through the state pre-copy (pre-copy source = the null slot).

## Fix

- Materialize the next state page when lookahead extends a page-aligned main-model sequence (both `get_num_blocks_to_allocate` and `allocate_new_blocks`), so the boundary token's state write has a real block.
- Derive the null padding from `num_tokens_main_model`, not the lookahead-inflated `num_tokens`, so the reserved page can never displace the running-state column.
- Grow the allocation budget by one when the next page is materialized.

## Testing

- Verified on a 4-node Thor SM110 cluster with GLM-5.3-Flash (NVFP4, MTP spec decode, prefix caching, chunked prefill): before the fix, deterministic 0% acceptance on boundary-ending chunks; after, the full prompt-size ladder and a 22-turn multi-turn conversation (360k prompt tokens) are coherent with mean acceptance length ~3.
- `num_tokens == num_tokens_main_model` (no lookahead) keeps the original padding math exactly.

items.title: [Bug] Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (qwen4_exp) + MTP: episodic 0% draft acceptance + repetition collapse in thinking block until max_tokens (SM120, bf16 KV, nightly @73029d4)
items.body:
### Summary

`Qwen3.8-Flash-Next` (qwen4_exp / QSA+GDN hybrid, ModelOpt **NVFP4** checkpoint) served with **MTP speculative decoding** (`num_speculative_tokens: 3`) intermittently collapses into a **spec-decode state-divergence episode**: per-window MTP draft acceptance drops to exactly **0** (~2,000 drafted, 0 accepted), generation pins to the 1-token/step spec-decode floor (~66 tok/s vs 95–135 tok/s healthy at 50–85% acceptance on the same pod), and the model emits an **endless repetition loop inside the thinking block** (`finish_reason=length` after burning the entire token budget — one request ran 4h57m to the 1M-token window). Episodes last hours, then recover fully. Not context-length-bound, not GPU/host-health-bound, not pod-age-bound.

**Critical cross-model signal:** a second, architecturally unrelated model on the **same image** with the **same MTP config** — Gemma 4 26B (NVFP4, thinking on) — failed its garbage probe the same day with the identical signature ("finish_reason=length … repetition collapse"). Two different checkpoints, one engine build, same failure mode ⇒ engine-level MTP/spec-decode state bug, not a model-weight or quant issue.

### Environment

- vLLM: `0.28.1rc1.dev278`, nightly base commit `73029d42441321b631779db3475031f5ec26dd6c` (first nightly containing in-tree qwen4_exp support, PR #53896, merged 2026-08-31)
- GPU: 2× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120), TP=2 (`g7e.12xlarge`)
- Model: `Inferact/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` (model_type `qwen4_exp`), thinking ON
- Spec: `--speculative-config {"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}` (in-checkpoint MTP head)
- KV cache: bf16/auto (QSA path is bf16-only), prefix caching on (~96% hit), `mamba-cache-mode align`, attention block 1600 tokens
- `--hf-overrides` YaRN rope scaling to 1M context
- Sampling defaults from checkpoint `generation_config`: temp 1.0, top_k 20, top_p 0.95, no repetition/presence penalty

### Fingerprint (full /metrics scrape, 10s windows, over the pod's life — 2,923 windows)

| signal | value |
|---|---|
| lifetime draft acceptance | 20% (5.35M drafted / 1.09M accepted) |
| healthy windows | acceptance 50–85%, solo stream 95–135 tok/s |
| collapse windows | acceptance **exactly 0.000/0.000/0.000** per position (~2,000 drafted), generation flat **64–70 tok/s** (the K=0 spec-decode floor: n=3 draft passes + 4-token verify per 1 accepted token) |
| hourly acceptance (NZ) | 02–07h 51–78% → 08h 31% → 09h 8% → 10h 12% → 11h 27% → 12h 4% → 13h 11% → **14h 66%** → 15h 18% → 16h 60% |
| worst request | started ~34k ctx, acceptance 28%→21%→**0% within 40s of prefill**, then flat 66 tok/s for **4h57m** until it hit the 1M window; client never disconnected |
| context independence | episodes at 1–2% KV **and** ~680k ctx; a 665k-ctx request during the same period had normal acceptance |
| health | GPUs max clock, 0 ECC, no throttle, no swap, PSI zero, 0 aborts/preemptions, KV pool never past 43% |
| finish | runaways end only via `finish_reason=length` (repetition collapse inside `<think>`; the thinking-end token is never emitted) |

### What was ruled out

- Context length (episodes at 1% and 20% KV; healthy 665k-ctx request in the same window)
- Pod age / monotonic drift (14h of full recovery mid-life)
- GPU or host health (all counters clean)
- Temperature-0 probes passed all day — collapse is tied to the default thinking-mode sampling, and only visible in the thinking block

### Engine-state suspects (both present at boot on this build)

1. `kv_cache_utils.py:1893`: with MTP, **every KV group including the 4 mamba/QSA recurrent groups is treated as a draft group and "prefix-cache reuse across requests will be disabled"** — yet main groups keep hitting the prefix cache at 96%. Draft-group and main-group state can therefore diverge on cache-hit requests.
2. **Fused multi-step draft decode is unsupported for `QWEN4_EXP_EXP_QSA_STATE`** — vLLM falls back to rebuilding attention metadata between draft steps. That fallback path (per-step metadata rebuild + QSA raw-key ring bookkeeping) is where a per-request state divergence would live.
3. Observed with both MTP@3 and co-batched traffic; zero-acceptance means drafter and target permanently disagree for the affected request — consistent with corrupted/divergent recurrent or cache state for that request, not the model "wandering" (a repeating loop is trivially predictable by a healthy drafter).

### Related upstream (same disease family, all still open)

- #47194 — hybrid + prefix cache + MTP3 correctness collapse (tool-call leak / needle recall) — fix PR #47861 closed **unmerged**
- #52475 — MTP repetition collapse on SM120 (Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 hybrid GDN) with quantized KV
- #53180 — MTP + hybrid GDN silently degenerate output (stock v0.27.1)
- #50837 — Qwen3.5 DFlash repetitive/degenerate output
- #39273 — ngram spec decode corrupted output on hybrid GDN
- qwen4_exp decode-correctness cluster: #54521 (non-deterministic prefill near indexer budget), #54739 (corrupted orthography), #54552/#54912 (QSA ring vs spec depth)
- llama.cpp side, same model family: ggml-org/llama.cpp#28158 (MTP/DFlash emits OOB token id), #28286 (draft-MTP cross-slot contamination under --parallel>1) — speculative-decode state bugs on this arch are not vLLM-specific

Note: the base model itself has a documented tendency for endless repetition in thinking mode at its default sampling (model card recommends presence_penalty 0–2) — we treat that as the **amplifier** (it's what degenerate state looks like in content), not the cause: it cannot explain 0/2,000 acceptance across two unrelated checkpoints on one build.

### Ask

- Any known interaction/fix between the MTP draft-group prefix-cache disable and QSA/mamba align-mode recurrent-state reuse?
- Is the `QWEN4_EXP_EXP_QSA_STATE` multi-step fallback (attention-metadata rebuild between draft steps) known to have correctness issues?
- We can provide the raw state dump (boot log, serve args, full metrics counters, acceptance-by-KV-bucket tables) and can A/B `speculative` off and an MTP-off restart on request; `/metrics`-based acceptance-rate telemetry for both affected models is available for plotting against the rollout.

### Impact

Production-quality bug: silent, hours-long runaway generations to the 1M-token window (~66 tok/s × 5h ≈ 1.2M tokens of billed-but-worthless output per incident), invisible except in the thinking block or spec-decode acceptance telemetry.

items.title: [Bug]: GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4 on B300: CUDA illegal access persists with MTP disabled; blocking/eager reports persistent_topk
items.body:
## Summary

We observed repeated CUDA illegal-memory-access failures serving GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4 on a single 8×B300 node. Disabling multi-token prediction (MTP), switching the MoE backend to FlashInfer CUTLASS, and subsequently using TP4 with BF16 KV cache did not yield a stable configuration.

These are the same symptom class, not a proven common root cause. All attached experimental runs used Dynamo 1.5's vLLM worker wrapper and native frontend. We have not validated a bare-vLLM reproduction with these synthetic inputs and cannot exclude integration or environment effects.

Potentially related: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54317 . That report uses a different hardware/build configuration. Please advise whether this evidence belongs there or warrants a separate issue.

## Environment

- Single node: 8× NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC; compute capability 10.3; driver 580.178.04.
- Model: nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4; revision 09b04e5e74bca08ca8549fc736d4cdd8624bfde3.
- Worker image: docker.io/vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:0674a3ea3c971706cea310bca71daadff68ea1717c758d2f54affa5def001b86.
- This digest matched the Linux/AMD64 child of vllm/vllm-openai:glm53-flash when checked on October 2; the digest, not the mutable tag, identifies our image.
- Live vLLM build: 0.28.1rc1.dev580+g385dce36b.
- Earlier same-image runtime snapshot: torch 2.13.0+cu130; flashinfer-python 0.6.18. These are not a fresh complete environment dump from the latest run.
- ai-dynamo==1.5.0 installed at worker startup; transitive dependencies were not fully pinned. A protobuf/CUTLASS-DSL dependency warning was present; its relevance is unknown.
- No LMCache or external/offloaded KV cache in these tests.

## Observed failures

1. Default FlashInfer TRTLLM MoE, 4×TP2 engines, expert parallelism, NVFP4 weights, FP8 KV and MTP3: illegal access reported while initializing a TMA descriptor via trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe. Complete pre-crash logs were lost; only a surviving excerpt is included.
2. CUTLASS MoE, otherwise the same settings: illegal access reported in KDA's chunk_kda_scaled_dot_kkt_fwd_kernel_intra_sub_inter. This occurred in concurrency-16 warmup for the second planned concurrency-32 run.
3. CUTLASS MoE with MTP disabled, FP8 KV and 4×TP2: four concurrency-32 repeats completed; the fifth failed. Detection was at copy_event.synchronize in output handling, not an identified originating kernel.
4. Same MTP-off setup plus CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 and --enforce-eager: three concurrency-32 repeats completed; the fourth failed. Both TP ranks reported torch.ops._C.persistent_topk, /workspace/csrc/libtorch_stable/topk.cu:227, in GLM's sparse-attention indexer. This is a vLLM custom C++ operator, not a FlashInfer MoE kernel. Blocking improves localization but does not itself prove where corruption originated.
5. Latest test: 2×TP4 engines, expert parallelism, CUTLASS MoE, NVFP4, BF16 KV, MTP disabled, ordinary nonblocking/graph execution. Startup and API smoke test succeeded, but the first concurrency-16 warmup failed. Both engines reported illegal access along build_prefill_chunk_metadata → _BUILD_PREFILL_CHUNK_METADATA_KERNEL → Triton load_binary. The exception occurred during Triton binary/handle initialization; this is not proof that the metadata kernel performed the illegal write. It is not a KDA or persistent_topk traceback.

A FlashInfer CUTEDSL alternative was also rejected at startup because of the unquantized MTP layer. That rejection was a compatibility failure, not a CUDA illegal-access reproduction.

Latest failure: 2026-10-05 18:21:33 UTC. Of 32 warmup requests, 17 returned HTTP 200 and 15 returned HTTP 503. No measured concurrency-32 requests or full repeats completed. We have no validated workaround and output correctness remains unverified.

## Workload and configuration

The attachments contain synthetic code-like prompts, not customer requests. Each prompt has approximately 125,011 chat-templated input tokens and requests 400 output tokens. There are two reusable prefix groups with approximately 107,499 prefix tokens; this gives an approximately 86% theoretical reuse ceiling, not a guaranteed measured hit rate.

Original benchmark: AIPerf 0.11 with a request-journaling proxy. Each repeat uses 32 warmup requests at concurrency 16, then 128 measured requests at concurrency 32; caches are not reset between repeats. Proxy-observed latency is not directly comparable with direct-client benchmarks.

Request payload: POST /v1/chat/completions, model=zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash, one user message containing the dataset text, stream=true, stream_options={"include_usage":true}, max_completion_tokens=400, ignore_eos=true, temperature=0.

Latest worker settings include TP4, EP enabled, modelopt_fp4, dtype=bfloat16, kv_cache_dtype=bfloat16, max_model_len=1048576, max_num_seqs=48, max_num_batched_tokens=65536, kv_cache_memory=123480309760, chunked prefill and prefix caching enabled, moe_backend=flashinfer_cutlass, no speculative-config and no enforce-eager. Full engine flags and environment are in deployment.sanitized.yaml.

The sanitized deployment is a review template, not a directly validated reproducer: namespace, storage and cluster placement must be supplied. The frozen datasets preserve the actual synthetic request text. We have not minimized the workload or independently validated an upstream standalone reproduction.

## Request to maintainers

Could the GLM/vLLM kernel owners investigate these failures and advise on a supported fix or workaround preserving NVFP4? In particular, please triage the persistent_topk traceback reproduced with MTP disabled, launch blocking and eager execution, and the newer TP4/BF16-KV traceback. If a smaller reproducer or Compute Sanitizer capture is required, please specify the exact configuration and evidence needed.

## Attachments

A sanitized evidence ZIP has been prepared for attachment through GitHub’s web interface (not uploaded by this connector). It includes sanitized traceback blocks for every retained failure site, the surviving default-MoE excerpt, a sanitized latest request journal and summary, environment details, a sanitized deployment template, and frozen synthetic warmup/measured datasets with checksums. It does not contain raw customer logs, customer prompts, internal cluster identifiers or credentials. No Xid-based hardware-fault conclusion is established by this package.
[glm53-nvfp4-cuda-evidence.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33078180/glm53-nvfp4-cuda-evidence.zip)

items.title: [Bug]: Qwen3.6 hybrid model with prefix caching + MTP3 causes tool-call leakage and needle recall failure, while no-MTP path is correct[错误]：
items.body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text Your output of `python collect_env.py` here ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug ### Summary When serving a Qwen3.6/Qwen3.5-style hybrid model with vLLM prefix caching and MTP3 speculative decoding enabled, the engine shows severe correctness regressions on cache-hit paths. The no-MTP hard-cache path works correctly with high prefix-cache hit rate. The MTP3 hard-cache path still gets cache hits, but tool calling, multi-turn tool use, and long-context needle recall fail. This looks related to hybrid full-attention + Mamba/GDN prefix-cache state reuse under speculative decoding, rather than a model-template-only issue. ### Environment Hardware: * 2 × RTX 2080 Ti 22GB * Turing / SM75 * Tensor parallel: 2 Model: * Qwopus3.6-27B-Coder-GPTQ-Pro * Qwen3.6 / Qwen3.5-style hybrid architecture * GPTQ-Pro / gptq_marlin path Serving: * OpenAI-compatible vLLM server * Tool parser: qwen3_coder * Reasoning parser: qwen3 * enable_thinking=false * CUDA graphs enabled * Prefix caching enabled * Prefix hash algorithm: sha256_cbor * KV cache dtype: fp8_e5m2 * MTP: 3 speculative tokens Please note: I intentionally avoided TurboQuant KV for this reproduction. The failing setup uses fp8_e5m2 KV. ### What works Hard-cache without MTP works correctly. Configuration: * fp8_e5m2 KV * prefix cache enabled * MTP/speculative decoding disabled Observed results: * vLLM engine prefix cache hit rate around 90-98% * real ClaudeCode/OpenClaw-style payload with about 58K static prefix hits correctly * cold prefill around 6s, hot prefill around 0.05s * streaming first-token latency improves strongly: * 58K long conversation: 19.31s cold to 3.40s hot * 8K tool request: 3.09s cold to 1.31s hot * 60K rich context: 11.58s cold to 4.12s hot * tool calling works * needle recall 10K/30K works * no content leak * no reasoning leak * no `` text leak * no repetition/star leakage ### What fails The same hard-cache setup fails after enabling MTP3. Configuration: * fp8_e5m2 KV * prefix cache enabled * MTP3 enabled * same model * same parser * same prompt/template path * same CUDA graphs path Observed results: * server starts successfully * prefix cache still works * 58K static prefix hit rate around 83.9% * cold PP 23.35s to hot avg 2.03s, about 91.3% reduction * no engine crash But correctness regresses badly: * tool call 10x: only 2/10 pass * multicase 18x: only 1/18 pass * needle recall 10K/30K: 0/10 pass * multi-turn tool use: 0/5 pass * `` XML leaks as plain text * repetition appears in at least one case * tool parser does not populate valid tool_calls reliably ### Why this looks like a vLLM prefix-cache + speculative decoding issue The failure only appears when MTP3 is combined with prefix caching on this hybrid model path. Important observations: * no-MTP + prefix cache works * fp8_e5m2 KV + prefix cache works * MTP3 starts and generates text * cache hit rate remains high * failures appear on structured/tool-call and recall tasks * the failing behavior resembles unsafe cache/state reuse rather than normal model quality degradation This seems related to prior hybrid prefix-cache + speculative decoding work, including: * unsafe prefix-cache hit with hybrid full-attention + Mamba/GDN models when EAGLE/MTP is enabled * Qwen3 tool parser / reasoning parser edge cases involving `` * speculative decoding interacting with structured outputs ### Expected behavior Prefix caching should be behavior-preserving. Enabling MTP3 should not change whether: * tool_calls are parsed correctly * `` appears only as structured tool call, not plain text * needle recall succeeds * multi-turn tool use works If MTP3 cannot safely reuse prefix-cached hybrid Mamba/GDN states, vLLM should either: 1. avoid unsafe hits, 2. disable the unsupported path with a clear warning, 3. or correctly roll back / verify speculative KV and Mamba/GDN state. ### Actual behavior MTP3 + prefix cache produces cache-hit speedups but breaks correctness: * tool-call text leakage * missing tool_calls * needle recall failure * multi-turn tool failure * occasional repetition ### Reproduction outline 1. Start vLLM with Qwen3.6/Qwen3.5-style hybrid model. 2. Enable prefix caching. 3. Use fp8_e5m2 KV. 4. Enable qwen3_coder tool parser and qwen3 reasoning parser. 5. Use a long static prefix, about 58K tokens, with dynamic suffix changes. 6. Warm the prefix cache. 7. Verify cache hits. 8. Run: * tool call prompt, 10 repetitions * multicase tool-call prompt, 18 repetitions * needle recall at 10K/30K * multi-turn tool use 9. Compare no-MTP vs MTP3. No-MTP passes. MTP3 fails. ### Request Could maintainers clarify whether Qwen3.6/Qwen3.5 hybrid Mamba/GDN prefix caching is expected to be compatible with MTP speculative decoding? If this is known to require recent fixes, which PRs or commits should be backported? I am especially interested in fixes around: * hybrid prefix-cache hit computation * Mamba/GDN state checkpoint reuse * speculative decoding rollback / verification with prefix cache * Qwen3 coder/XML tool parser interaction with speculative decoding * reasoning parser handling of `` lookahead ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.title: [Bug]: `prompt_logprobs` silently corrupted for some requests when MTP speculative decoding is enabled (Qwen3.5-family, chunked prefill; two builds, two checkpoints)
items.body:
### Your current environment

- **Hardware**: NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, compute capability 12.1, aarch64, 121 GiB unified memory), single GPU
- **Build A**: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-aarch64` — vLLM `0.26.1rc1.dev1102+ge9d1398d9`, flashinfer 0.6.17, torch 2.13.0+cu130
- **Build B** (independent source build, community image): vLLM `0.27.2rc0` @ `7f7a32c`, flashinfer 0.6.16.post3
- **Models** (both Qwen3.8-27B, hybrid GDN linear attention, each shipping its own MTP head):
  - `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` (ModelOpt MIXED_PRECISION, fp8 KV)
  - `cyankiwi/Qwen3.8-27B-AWQ-BF16-INT4` (compressed-tensors W4A16)

### 🐛 Describe the bug

With MTP speculative decoding enabled (`--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'`), the `prompt_logprobs` returned by `/v1/completions` are **wildly wrong for a subset of requests** — with no error, no warning, HTTP 200 — while the identical server **without** `--speculative-config` scores every request correctly.

Setup: a fixed corpus split into 8 chunks (server-reported input tokens 1714 / 457 / 480 / 525 / 666 / 599 / 822 / 975), each scored with

```json
POST /v1/completions
{"model": "...", "prompt": "<chunk>", "max_tokens": 1, "temperature": 0, "prompt_logprobs": 0}
```

sent sequentially in that order. Sum of per-token logprobs per chunk:

| chunk | tokens | plain NVFP4 (A) | **MTP NVFP4 (A)** | plain INT4 (A) | **MTP INT4 (A)** | plain NVFP4 (B) | **MTP NVFP4 (B)** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 1714 | −3241.5 | −3219.0 | −3157.0 | −3157.5 | −3224.3 | −3236.5 |
| **1** | **457** | −586.2 | **−8439.9** | −574.1 | **−6054.5** | −583.8 | **−5352.4** |
| **2** | **480** | −993.9 | **−6027.7** | −984.2 | **−9950.1** | −982.4 | **−9910.5** |
| 3 | 525 | −946.5 | −948.8 | −922.8 | −923.0 | −950.8 | −938.3 |
| 4 | 666 | −618.4 | −617.9 | −603.2 | −604.5 | −609.8 | −615.9 |
| 5 | 599 | −186.2 | −193.0 | −188.3 | −187.6 | −187.1 | −194.2 |
| 6 | 822 | −329.0 | −329.6 | −322.3 | −322.5 | −330.1 | −338.5 |
| 7 | 975 | −407.0 | −414.0 | −389.6 | −388.8 | −412.7 | −407.0 |
| **corpus PPL** | 6238 | **3.227** | **25.45** | **3.142** | **31.84** | **3.213** | **28.94** |

Observations:

1. **Exactly the same two chunks (1 and 2) are corrupted in every MTP run** — 3 runs, 2 checkpoints (two different quantization backends), 2 independent builds. Their mean NLL jumps from ~1.7 to **12.6–20.7 nats/token** (PPL 10⁵–10⁹), i.e. the logprobs look like they were computed against the wrong positions/context, not like a slightly worse model.
2. The other 6 chunks (85% of tokens) agree with the non-speculative server to 0.1–0.3%, so the model, weights and kernels are fine; recomputing PPL on those 6 chunks gives −0.12% / +0.02% / +0.29% vs plain — as expected, since prefill scoring should not depend on speculation at all.
3. Generation is unaffected: single-stream benchmarks, greedy token-match gates against the plain server and sanity prompts are all normal on the same MTP servers (acceptance ~3.8 tokens/step).
4. **The corruption is a property of the individual request, not of request order.** An isolation probe on a fourth checkpoint (`unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4`, MTP K=3, same server) gives:

   | probe | sequence sent | verdict |
   |---|---|---|
   | a | chunk 1 **alone** (fresh server, first request) | **polluted** |
   | b | chunk 0 (1715 tok) → chunk 1 | clean, **polluted** |
   | c | chunk 3 (526 tok) → chunk 1 | clean, **polluted** |
   | d | chunk 1 → chunk 1 (twice) | **polluted, polluted** |
   | e | chunk 0 (1715 tok) → chunk 3 | clean, clean |

   So it is neither "the request after a large one" nor a warm-up effect: chunk 1 is corrupted even as the very first request on a fresh server, and a large predecessor does not corrupt a chunk that is otherwise fine (probe e).

5. **Possible size threshold (hypothesis, only 2 samples — not scanned).** The corrupted chunks are the only two in the corpus below 512 prompt tokens: 457 and 480 scored tokens. Every clean chunk is ≥ 525 (525 / 666 / 599 / 822 / 975 / 1714). We have not swept prompt length to find an exact boundary, so we can only report the correlation, not a threshold.
6. SGLang on the same corpus, same checkpoints, with its MTP speculation enabled, returns `sum_logprob` bit-identical to its non-speculative server for all 8 chunks — so this is engine-side.

Startup log difference between the affected and unaffected servers (present on both builds, `vllm.py:1931` on A, `vllm.py:1844` on B):

```
WARNING [vllm.py:1931] max_num_scheduled_tokens is set to 2048 based on the speculative decoding settings. This may lead to suboptimal performance. Consider increasing max_num_batched_tokens to accommodate the additional tokens.
```

We first suspected an ordering/scheduling effect (the corrupted chunks follow the largest prompt), but probe (a)/(e) above rules that out. What remains consistent with the data is an interaction between the reduced per-step token budget under speculative decoding and the prompt-logprobs gathering path for **short prompts** — but we have not traced it in code, and the 512-token correlation rests on only two samples.

Serve flags common to all rows: `--max-model-len 32768 --no-enable-prefix-caching --kv-cache-dtype fp8` (NVFP4 rows) / auto (INT4), `--kv-cache-memory-bytes <pinned>`, default (non-eager) CUDA graphs, chunked prefill enabled by default. Affected rows add only `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'`.

### Reproduction

```bash
vllm serve RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 --max-model-len 32768 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --trust-remote-code \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
# Minimal case: send ONE short prompt (~450 tokens) as the very first request:
#   {"prompt": "<~450 tokens of text>", "max_tokens": 1, "temperature": 0, "prompt_logprobs": 0}
# Compare sum(prompt_logprobs) against the same server started WITHOUT --speculative-config.
# In our runs the short prompt's summed logprob is off by an order of magnitude
# (e.g. -578.9 plain vs -5352…-8440 with MTP), while prompts >= ~525 tokens agree to <0.3%.
```

We can share the exact 8-chunk corpus, the scoring script (stdlib-only) and all raw JSON responses.

### Expected behavior

`prompt_logprobs` should be independent of whether speculative decoding is enabled (it only affects the decode path); at minimum, a request whose prompt cannot be scored correctly under the reduced token budget should fail loudly rather than return plausible-looking garbage.

### Before submitting a new issue…

- [x] Searched issues/PRs for `prompt_logprobs` + speculative/MTP; only #50792 (PD-disaggregated OverflowError) is nearby and unrelated.

---

*Disclosure (added retroactively, per the repository's `AGENTS.md`): this work was carried out with AI assistance — investigation, measurement scripting, and drafting. The hardware, the runs, the logs and every number above are real and reproducible; the account owner reviewed and approved the content before it was posted, and can defend it end-to-end. Raw artifacts are available on request.*
